source_of_truth: Derived by hand from the build I wrote. Three routes in one build: (1) /heavy lists heavy-vendor.js (300000 raw, 227 KB gzip) async:false -> in the initial set -> a genuine initial-weight defect; (2) /editor lists lazy-editor.js (300000 raw, 227 KB gzip) async:true -> deferred, initial set ~21 KB -> correct code-splitting, not a defect; (3) /orphan is in routes-manifest with no client-reference manifest -> attribution genuinely unavailable [info]. The single defect-level signal expected is route-heavy-initial-chunk on /heavy only; it must not fire on /editor or /orphan.

expected.rationale: heavy-vendor.js (221.9 KB gzip) is in /heavy's initial set (async:false) and exceeds the 150 KB single-chunk threshold; line is null as the finding is path-attributed.

forbidden.why_not_a_defect: the large editor chunk is async:true (lazy), excluded from /editor's initial set; firing would be a false positive on correct code-splitting.
/orphan has no client-reference manifest, so there is no initial set to measure; any heavy claim would be invented.
